text: DSH Plugin Scout 是 DSH 网页客户端的插件发现工具，在官方 Plugins 页面增加 Scout 标签页，并在插件详情中显示评分与核验项目。它从 GitHub 的 dsh-plugin 主题和 npm 获取插件元数据，将插件按用途分类，提供关键词搜索、兼容性及来源筛选、排序和分页，并支持查看详情与已安装状态。用户可手动刷新索引，也可配置 GitHub 凭证后进行更新；插件安装仍由 DSH 官方安装器处理。

DSH Plugin Scout adds a Scout tab to DSH web Plugins, where users can search, categorize, filter, sort, and inspect plugins. It refreshes metadata from GitHub and npm and shows compatibility checks; the official DSH installer handles installation.

Find DSH plugins and narrow the list by compatibility or source
DSH Plugin Scout 的功能「插件目录筛选」：在 Plugins → Scout 搜索插件，并按用途、兼容性、来源或已安装状态筛选结果；列表支持排序、分页和打开详情。
DSH Plugin Scout 的功能「索引刷新与详情核验」：在 Scout 页查看插件详情与评分核验项，并通过 GitHub 凭证触发索引刷新；安装操作交由官方插件安装器。
DSH Plugin Scout 查询 GitHub GraphQL 与 npm 的公开插件元数据；刷新索引需 GitHub Token 或 gh CLI 登录。（见 src/auth.mjs:19-23）

[](https://github.com/fegnze/dsh-plugin-scout/actions/workflows/ci.yml) · MIT

Discover and verify DeepSeek Harness plugins published under the GitHub topic `dsh-plugin`, from inside DSH. Plugins are grouped by purpose, ranked by trust score, and checked against the official peer-compatibility rule. Supports DSH **0.2.x** (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`); tested on desktop 0.2.0-rc.2.

dsh-plugin-scout README · DSH Plugin Scout：> The in-app UI is currently Chinese only. The plugin's title and description in the official Plugins page are localized (`locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json`).

dsh-plugin-scout README · Install：Open the official **Plugins** page → **Add plugin**, and enter one of:

| Spec | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh-plugin-scout` | Recommended. Prebuilt npm package with provenance; no install scripts, no build approval needed |
| Absolute path of a prebuilt `dsh-plugin-scout-<version>.tgz`, if supplied with a release | Bypasses the npm registry; the current tag workflow creates release notes only and does not attach a tarball |

dsh-plugin-scout README · Install：From the CLI: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-plugin-scout`. Enable it on the Plugins page, then open **Plugins → Scout**. The tab is labeled **Scout** in both languages; no sidebar entry is added. The official **Discover** tab is unchanged.

Do not install from `github:fegnze/dsh-plugin-scout`: a git install fetches source without `lib/`, and this repository deliberately ships no `prepare` script.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Native Discover index：Add this URL in the official **Plugins → Discover → Index sources** dialog:

```text
https://fegnze.github.io/dsh-plugin-scout/index.json
```

This is a format-1 catalog, not an embedded Scout page. You do not need to install Scout to browse it. GitHub Actions rebuilds it daily at 03:23 UTC and on generator changes, then deploys only after the official DSH validator accepts the document. Failed generation leaves the previous deployment intact.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Native Discover index：The public catalog contains deduplicated npm bundles compatible with the target DSH 0.2.1-rc.2, with a matching repository, no install hooks, and advertised provenance. Archived, risky, version-drifted, stale or incomplete entries are excluded. Forks retain a source label. Provenance presence is not cryptographic verification or a security guarantee. Each entry pins the npm version and uses npm's real release time; the official installer remains the final authority. The target runtime is a publishing policy, not a compatibility claim for every DSH release.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Native Discover index：Generate from public GitHub/npm data with `GH_TOKEN=<read-only-token> node scripts/generate-market.mjs`. `MARKET_OUTPUT`, `SCOUT_CACHE`, and `DSH_TARGET` override the output, disposable crawl cache, and target runtime. No local profile or user cache is published. The generated `site/index.json` and crawl cache are ignored by Git; CI uploads only the public catalog as the Pages artifact. Adding the source remains your explicit action; Scout does not alter configured index sources.

dsh-plugin-scout README · One-click install, through the official installer：The **Install** button in the details drawer takes the same path as the official **Add plugin**: `inspect` first, then `installBundle(spec, {enabled: false, requestId, registry})`. Installed plugins start **disabled**; **Enable** is a separate click (`setBundleEnabled`).
section: One-click install, through the official installer

dsh-plugin-scout README · One-click install, through the official installer：- Plugins with install hooks, or whose DSH peers do not cover the running version, need a second click to install.
- When the official installer blocks dependency build scripts (`pendingBuilds`), they are listed by name; a double click on **Allow and reinstall** retries with `approvedBuilds`.
- **Cancel install** calls `cancelInstall` with the same `requestId`; a lost reply is recovered with `waitForInstall`. On failure the official installer restores `package.json` and the lockfile.
- **Uninstalling and version exemptions stay on the official Plugins page.** Scout never calls `removeBundle`; the tests fail if it does. Without the official `pluginManager`, the Install button is hidden and the drawer falls back to "copy pinned spec + open the Plugins page".
section: One-click install, through the official installer

dsh-plugin-scout README · Data sources (first-party only)：| Source | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub GraphQL `search(topic:dsh-plugin)` | Repository metadata, root `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml` text (never evaluated) |
| `registry.npmjs.org/<name>/latest` | The manifest that would actually be installed: peers, install hooks, `repository`, provenance |
| Official `pluginManager.listBundles` / `inspect` | Installed state; the official pre-install check (resolves only, runs no code) |
| Official `pluginManager.installBundle` / `waitForInstall` / `cancelInstall` / `setBundleEnabled` | One-click install (disabled by default), cancel, separate enable; progress from `plugin-manager/install-state` and `install-log` events |

dsh-plugin-scout README · Data sources (first-party only)：No third-party marketplace or aggregator is used. Topic searches explicitly use `fork:true` to include both original repositories and forks; forks retain their source notice and undergo the same checks. After upgrading from 0.1.5 or earlier, use **Rebuild full index** once to discover older forks omitted by the previous search scope.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Data sources (first-party only)：**Crawling, measured (2026-10):** the topic holds about 19,000 repositories, 12,700 of them created in August, many of them same-name copies. GitHub search returns at most 1,000 results per query, so Scout bisects time windows adaptively (≤900 results per window, 60 s minimum window). Pages are 50 items: 100-item pages return 502 in dense windows, so on 502 the page size steps down to 25, then 10, resuming from the same cursor. Later runs crawl incrementally by `pushed`.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Data sources (first-party only)：**Refresh is streaming and pays only for what changed:**
- **Newest first.** Windows are seeded geometrically (last 6 h / 1 d / 3 d / 1 w / 1 mo / 3 mo / older) and paged from the newest. Window counting and paging overlap (3 workers).
- **Publish while crawling.** Each page is merged into the record set immediately and published every 1.5 s; the UI reloads the list when `status.rev` changes. The previous index stays usable throughout. A checkpoint is written every 30 s.
- **Pay for change.** With an existing index, a light query fetches metadata only (100 per page, no blobs). Repositories whose `pushedAt` is unchanged keep their facts and only refresh stars and similar metadata; changed ones fetch `package.json` and the patch by node id in batches of 50.
- **npm in parallel.** npm lookups run alongside the GitHub crawl (8 workers), only for repositories with new pushes, missing entries, or entries older than one day. Entries older than one day are refreshed oldest first, at most 800 per run, even when the repository was not seen in that incremental crawl.
- **Canonical source recovery.** A refresh also follows same-name npm

dsh-plugin-scout README · Data sources (first-party only)：Measured on 2026-10-14 over a real network:

| Scenario | First results | Total | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incremental, 1,082 repos pushed | 4.5 s | 38 s | 125 refetched blobs, 963 metadata-only, 70 npm lookups |
| Cold full crawl | 6.7 s | — | ~1,000 plugins browsable within 60 s; the rest fill in the background |

dsh-plugin-scout README · Checks and trust score：| Check | Rule | Points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V1 | Root `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle` / `dsh.client` (otherwise not a plugin) | 20 |
| V2 | Official peer rule: only `@deepseek-ai/dsh` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`, `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, {includePrerelease})`, `workspace:*` means the running version. Inside the App, Scout calls `dsh-app-boot.evaluatePluginCompatibility` directly | covered 30 · no peers 10 · not covered 5 |
| V3 | Install hooks: preinstall / install / postinstall / prepare | none +15 · present −15 |
| V4 | Source chain: the same-name npm package's `repository` points back to this repo | match +15 · mismatch −20 · unpublished 0 |
| V5 | npm provenance | +10 |
| V6 | Activity: archived, pushed within 90 days, version drift (V6b) | +5 / −10 |
| V9 | Uses the `@deepseek-ai/` scope but the repo is not owned by deepseek-ai | −30 |
| V10 | Fork | note only |
| — | Stars: `min(5, round(log10(1+s)·2))` | ≤5 |

dsh-plugin-scout README · Checks and trust score：The total is clamped to 0–100. Any ✕ marks the plugin as **risky**: copying its spec or installing it takes two clicks, and its badge shows ✕. Repositories sharing a package name collapse under one representative, chosen by: matching source chain > score > stars > earliest creation. The rest are listed as copies, hidden by default.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Checks and trust score：Ten purpose categories: UI, session, memory, agent, tools, models, security, development, bridges, domain. A category is scored from the official packages a plugin depends on (highest weight), topics/keywords (3), and text (2); a plugin is categorized only with a score of at least 2. On 41 hand-labelled plugins, the top-1 category is correct for at least 35.

dsh-plugin-scout README · UI and integration points：- **Scout tab:** **Plugins → Scout**, contributed through `plugins.tab` (`id: dsh-plugin-scout`, `order: 40`), with search, filters (compatibility, risk, kind, installed state, copies), category chips, sorting and paging. There is no sidebar entry or separate `main` panel. The official Plugins page owns the heading; Scout adds no duplicate page title or subtitle. Scout fits the remaining viewport height: plugin results scroll independently below the category and sort controls, and overflowing filters have their own scroll area. Wheel scrolling at either area's boundary does not propagate to the page. The official **Discover** tab remains unchanged.
- **Pagination:** defaults to descending star count, with 60 plugins per page; enter a valid page number and click **Jump** or press Enter to go directly to it; **Previous / Next** and page/total counts stay below the independently scrolling results. Changing search, filters, category or sort returns to page 1 and resets the results' scroll position after loading; explicit page navigation also resets scroll. dsh-plugin-scout README · Development：```sh
npm install --ignore-scripts
npm test          # builds lib/, then runs the core / host / client / manifest suites
```

Local debugging: add this directory's absolute path on the Plugins page (a link install; do not move the directory). Host changes need a full App restart; client-only changes need a window reload.

dsh-plugin-scout README · GitHub setup：Open **Scout → GitHub settings**. First use without a credential shows setup automatically; an existing index remains browsable. Enter a GitHub personal access token, click **Save**, then **Check connection** and **Refresh index**. The check is a read-only GraphQL request, not a crawl. Use a token that can read public repository metadata through GitHub GraphQL; do not grant private-repository or write access solely for Scout. Invalid/expired credentials, permission denial, rate limits and network failures are reported without upstream response bodies.

dsh-plugin-scout README · GitHub setup：The Host saves the Token through the official DSH credentials service under the fixed reference `DSH_SCOUT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, not ordinary plugin configuration or the index. **The local provider stores plaintext in an owner-permission credential file; it is not encryption or Keychain.** Token input is transient, cleared after save and never put in browser storage. Saved Tokens are never returned by the API. **Clear saved Token** removes this reference's stored value only; environment or CLI fallbacks may still provide a credential. Older hosts without the credentials service cannot save Tokens and should use CLI/environment setup.

dsh-plugin-scout README · GitHub setup：Alternatively install [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/), manually run `gh auth login --hostname github.com` on the same machine/account running DSH, then return to **Check connection**. Scout does not launch login or open authentication pages automatically. The existing CLI lookup checks common Homebrew/system paths; a nonstandard installation may require environment setup instead.

dsh-plugin-scout README · GitHub setup：Credential order: DSH credentials for `DSH_SCOUT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (stored value before that reference's ambient fallbacks), process environment `DSH_SCOUT_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN`, then `gh auth token` via DSH subprocess. Environment variables must be present **when DSH starts**: exporting one in a later terminal does not update the running desktop App. Changes saved through DSH credentials take effect on the next operation without restarting.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Data and configuration：- Index: `~/.dsh/dsh-plugin-scout/index.json` stores facts only (repo metadata, slimmed manifests, npm cache) and is re-judged against the current runtime on every load, so compatibility verdicts follow DSH upgrades automatically.
- Optional config: `dataDir`, `topic`, `runtimeVersion` (overrides runtime detection), `autoRefresh` (boolean, default `true`), `autoRefreshHours` (hours, default `1`). Set `autoRefresh: false` to disable automatic refresh; `autoRefreshHours: 0` remains the legacy disable switch.
- **Host-only scheduling:** after a 45 s startup grace period and index loading, Scout checks whether the persisted `succeededAt` completion time is older than the configured interval, falling back to the legacy `crawledAt` crawl-start watermark when no completion clock exists. One in-process timeout checks each interval; missed intervals are not replayed. Scheduling lives only in the DSH Host, not the browser or a daemon; no LaunchAgent or external scheduler is created, and plugin disposal cancels the timeout.
- **Shared refresh path:** automatic refresh uses the existing default mode: incremental after `fullAt` exists, otherwise
dsh-plugin-scout README · Data and configuration：Automatic refresh has been manually accepted in the live DSH application. UI position preservation is covered by client regression tests.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Security boundaries：- Exact routes use official `connection.fetch` under `/api/dsh-plugin-scout/api/*`, shared by desktop and Web carriers. The carrier authenticates requests and refuses non-owner peers before dispatch; Scout additionally requires `x-dsh-plugin-scout: 1`. No independent loopback server or auth-token copying is used. The `connection` service is required.
- `cordis.patch.yml` is scanned for `name:` with a regex; YAML tags are never parsed. Crawled code is never executed and tarballs are never downloaded.
- Style tags carry `data-plugin` / `data-plugin-css` before entering the DOM. Only `--dsw-alias-*` tokens are used; class names avoid substrings that host skins target; the drawer does not use `role="dialog"`.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Layout：- `src/core/`: `classify.mjs` (categories), `verify.mjs` (checks and score), `crawl.mjs` (GraphQL, windows, npm), `store.mjs` (fact index, queries).
- `src/host.mjs`: runtime and token detection, refresh state machine, same-origin routes, in-process timer.
- `src/client/`: Discover page, drawer, installer, official-page badge/section, styles.
- `scripts/build.mjs`: esbuild bundling; both artifacts are **executed** after writing, as the gate.
- `test/`: `core` (real GraphQL page, 41 labelled samples), `host` (fake-fetch end-to-end refresh, route auth), `client` (Happy DOM loading the built artifact), `manifest` (official packaging conventions).
dsh-plugin-scout README · Layout：After a DSH upgrade, re-check the official Plugins page slot names, the `pluginManager` methods, and the `dsh-app-boot` exports before re-accepting.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Official conventions followed：Based on the official repository's `docs/user/develop/basic/publish`, `docs/cookbook/adding-a-package` §5, and the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-package-manifest` types; `test/manifest.test.mjs` asserts each one.

dsh-plugin-scout README · Official conventions followed：| Convention | This package |
| --- | --- |
| Bundle: `dsh.bundle.patch`; patch rows reference the package **by name** | `./cordis.patch.yml` → `name: 'dsh-plugin-scout'` |
| Only public author fields under `dsh` | `manifestVersion: 1`, `bundle`, `client` (`platform: web`) |
| Display metadata: `locale/en.json` is the entry, other languages use the same fields; export `./locale/*.json` and `./package.json`, and ship them | `meta.title` / `meta.description` in `en.json` and `zh.json` |
| Icon: relative path inside the package, ≤256 KiB, self-contained | `./icon.svg` |
| Packages sharing host instances are peers; the version gate reads only `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peers | `@deepseek-ai/cordis ~4.0.4`; `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot >=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0` (optional, declares the range for the official gate) |
| `engines.dsh` is declarative | `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0` |
| Ship prebuilt artifacts; never ask users to approve builds | Published to npm with `--provenance`; no `prepare` or other install hooks |

dsh-plugin-scout README · Releasing：1. Prepare the intended `version` in `package.json` and commit the release changes to `main`.
2. Manually dispatch `publish.yml` from `main` with `expected_sha` set to the full approved commit SHA. Keep `dry_run: true` (the default) for validation first: the workflow checks the SHA, installs dependencies without lifecycle scripts, runs tests (including the build), and previews the package with `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts`. A dry run does not publish. For an approved release, dispatch the same SHA with `dry_run: false` to run `npm publish --access public --provenance --ignore-scripts`.
3. npm authenticates through Trusted Publishing (OIDC), so no npm token is stored in the repository; provenance is attached automatically. Configure npmjs.com → package Settings → Trusted Publisher for this GitHub repository and workflow `publish.yml`, or use `npx npm@latest trust github dsh-plugin-scout --file publish.yml --repo fegnze/dsh-plugin-scout`.
